TRUST: JSW HR Operations Manual

i.

JSW Group and JSW Motors Vision and Foundation

JSW Group

Our Purpose

We accelerate the growth and prosperity of the communities we live in by.

Our Vision

Fostering a sustainable future by positively impacting people, communities, and the environment.

Our Values

Commitment

Staying true and delivering what we promise both internally and externally. Consistently striving to ensure results. Being honest and transparent in all our conduct and disclosures. Being responsive to the needs of our stakeholders. Going by the letter and the spirit of the law.

Courage

Dreaming big and challenging status quo. Setting high goals for ourselves with confidence and conviction. Trying innovative methods or solutions.

Agility

Accepting & managing changes and uncertainty with speed. Openness to learn and adapt.

Collaboration

To foster teamwork and inclusivity, recognising the strength that comes from diverse perspectives.

Compassion

Caring and being considerate about the impact of our actions on our people, environment and society. Promoting well-being of all, at and beyond work.

JSW Motors

Our Vision

Make world-class future-ready mobility, shaped for India powering a more confident, self-reliant India.

Our Foundation

The vision says where we are going. The foundation says what we do each day to get there.

Reliability

We do what we say, take ownership, and earn trust through every action.

Innovation with Purpose

We challenge convention, embrace change, and turn ideas into impact.

Indian Heart, Global Mind

We put India at the center - bringing the world's best to every Indian's reach.

Shared Future

We believe the future is co-created, and progress should empower everyone.

ii.

Message from Management

Message from Management (Option 1)

It gives me great pleasure to introduce the JSW Motors HR Operations Manual.

As a young brand, we have a unique opportunity to build the right culture, standards and ways of working from the very beginning. The choices we make today will shape the experience of our employees, dealer partners and customers for years to come.

At JSW Motors, we believe that great customer experiences are created by engaged, capable and confident people. When our employees feel supported, developed and valued, they bring that same commitment to every customer interaction.

This manual provides a strong framework for managing the employee lifecycle, from hiring and onboarding to development, performance, rewards and separation. It is designed to help our dealer partners build consistent people practices while ensuring a positive employee experience across the network.

This guide serves as a recommended standard, not a mandate. Our dealer partners remain the employer of record and retain full responsibility for employment decisions and legal compliance. Where stronger practices already exist, we encourage partners to continue and build upon them.

As we grow together, our success will be defined not only by the vehicles we sell, but by the trust we earn from our employees, partners and customers. We look forward to building a world-class dealer network founded on strong people practices and shared success.

Together, let's create a workplace and a customer experience that sets new standards for the industry.

[Name]
[Designation]
JSW Motors

Message from Management (Option 2)

When I think about what will make JSW Motors successful, I don't think about market share or sales targets first. I think about people.

Every great business is built on a simple truth: take care of your people and they will take care of everything else. It's not a strategy or a mantra—it's just how things work when you pay attention.

The employees walking into our dealerships each morning are carrying more than just their job responsibilities. They're carrying their aspirations, their families' hopes, their desire to be part of something worthwhile. How we respond to that - how we train them, support them when things get difficult, recognize their contributions, help them grow—that's the foundation we're building on.

This manual isn't about rules and procedures. It's about building the kind of workplace where people can do their best work. Where a young service advisor can see a path forward. Where a receptionist feels their role matters. Where a technician can take pride in their craft. Where a sales consultant feels he is bringing life to a customer’s dream of buying a car.

We're starting with a clean slate in JSW Motors and that's both exciting and humbling. We are standing at a point wherein we have a chance to get it right from day one - to create an environment where people want to come to work, where they feel valued and where they can see their future.

This guide gives our dealer partners the tools to build that foundation. The rest - the sales, the growth, the customer loyalty - will follow naturally.

At the end of the day, we're not really in the automobile business. We're in the people business. The cars are just what brings us together.

[Name]
[Designation]
JSW Motors

Message from Management (Option 3)

We're bringing something special to India with JSW Motors - a world-class product with a distinctly Indian heart. Everything about this brand has been crafted to meet global standards while staying true to what Indian customers value and deserve.

That same philosophy needs to come alive in how we build our teams. We have an incredible opportunity here: to create a dealer network where every employee embodies this blend of international excellence and local understanding. Where professionalism meets warmth. Where efficiency meets genuine care.

The market we're entering isn't just competitive - it's full of possibility. Customers today are more discerning, more informed and more willing to embrace brands that truly understand them. That's our opening. And the people in our dealerships are the ones who will turn that opportunity into reality.

Every employee - from the sales consultant to the service technician to the person answering phones - is carrying our brand reputation in their hands. They are the ones who will either build trust. They are the ones who turn a transaction into a relationship. They are the ones who create the experiences that customers remember.

This manual is designed to help our dealer partners create the conditions for those employees to succeed. Because when we invest in our people - when we give them proper training, clear expectations, growth opportunities and genuine support - they don't just work for us. They become advocates for our customers.

An employee who feels valued doesn't just show up for a pay check. They go the extra mile. They solve problems creatively. They make customers feel important because they know what that feels like themselves.

As we build the JSW Motors network across India, let's be clear about what we're really building: a community of professionals who are equipped, empowered and enthusiastic about creating exceptional customer experiences. That's the competitive advantage no one can copy.

Our people are the light that guides customers to us and keeps them with us. Let's make sure that light shines bright.

[Name]
[Designation]
JSW Motors

CHAPTER 1

Dealership Organisation Structure

"Structure follows strategy."
PURPOSE:
  • Provide dealer partners with an industry benchmarked organisation structure that is optimised as per outlet category
  • Set clear accountability and a formal reporting hierarchy
BENEFIT TO DEALERSHIPS:
  • Right-sized team and right person for the right job helps deliver optimum results with better profitability
BENEFIT TO CUSTOMERS:
  • Smooth and seamless customer journey
  • Consistent customer experience
  • Transparent communication

Principles

A robust organizational structure provides stability to the dealership operations through:

Role Clarity

  • Responsibilities are defined
  • Employees take accountability as per their roles

Efficient Decision Making

  • Correct hierarchy and decision tree
  • Communication flow via correct channels

Enhanced Collaboration

  • Effective delegation
  • Clear functional and operational reporting

Resource Optimization

  • Right person - right job
  • Higher productivity due to well-defined roles & responsibilities

    CHAPTER 2

    Job Descriptions

    "A good job description tells you what success looks like, not just what tasks to perform."
    PURPOSE:
    • To provide role-based clarity
    • Clearly establish responsibilities and KPIs
    BENEFIT TO DEALERSHIPS:
    • Improved operational efficiency
    • Faster decision making
    • Clear accountability
    BENEFIT TO CUSTOMER:
    • Customers get directed to the right expert
    • Faster resolution of queries
    • Consistent experience

    Principles

    • Fundamental requirements for each role
    • Defined core competencies
    • Clear KPIs in job description

    This chapter covers all roles required in the sales function of a JSW Motors dealership. Select any role from the list to view its full profile - department, reporting line, education and experience benchmarks, key responsibilities, KPIs and competencies.

    Leadership

    CEO

    DepartmentDealer Management
    Reporting toDealer Principal
    Role impactOverall P&L Ownership & Strategic Leadership
    DepartmentDealer Management
    Reporting toDealer Principal
    Role impactOverall P&L Ownership & Strategic Leadership

    Position Overview

    The CEO owns the dealership's overall P&L and strategic direction, leading sales, aftersales and value-added business functions to deliver profitable growth, brand governance and long-term stakeholder value in a vehicle retail environment.

    1. Education

    Graduate / MBA in Business Administration, Management, Engineering or related field.Additional certification in Automotive Retail Management or General Management preferred.

    2. Experience

    18–25 years of experience in automotive dealership operations or OEM-affiliated retail leadership, preferably in passenger car segment.Minimum 8–10 years in a CEO / Business Head / General Manager capacity with full P&L ownership.Exposure to PHEV, NEV, EV or new-technology vehicle retail operations strongly preferred.Proven track record of leading a multi-outlet, multi-brand or high-volume dealership group.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    1. Business Strategy & P&L Ownership

    2. Sales, Aftersales & Cross-Functional Operations Oversight

    3. OEM & Key Stakeholder Relationship Management

    4. New Energy Vehicle (PHEV/NEV) Business Readiness & Charging Infrastructure

    5. Financial Planning, Working Capital & Investment Management

    6. Talent Leadership & Organization Development

    7. Facility, Infrastructure & Regulatory Compliance

    8. Customer Experience & Brand Standards Governance

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    i. Business Performance
    • Overall dealership net profitability (%)
    • Revenue growth across sales, aftersales, F&I and VAS
    • Return on capital employed (ROCE)
    • Market share within territory
    ii. Sales & Aftersales Effectiveness
    • Sales target achievement (volume & value)
    • Service throughput and bay/workshop utilization
    • PHEV/NEV charging infrastructure readiness & uptime
    iii. Customer Experience
    • Sales Satisfaction Index (SSI)
    • Net Promoter Score (NPS)
    • Customer complaint resolution turnaround time
    iv. Financial Health
    • Working capital and inventory turnaround days
    • Debtor days and OEM claims/incentive realization
    v. People & Governance
    • Leadership team retention and bench strength
    • Statutory, OEM audit and process compliance score

    5. Key Competencies

    Strategic & Business AcumenP&L OwnershipOEM & Stakeholder ManagementPeople LeadershipChange Management (EV/NEV Transition)Financial AcumenCustomer CentricityDecision Making & Risk Management

    2. Sales Team Leadership & Development

    Position Overview

    The CFO leads the dealership's financial strategy, controllership and treasury functions, ensuring capital efficiency, statutory compliance and robust financial governance to support profitable growth in vehicle retail business.

    1. Education

    CA / ICWA / MBA (Finance) or equivalent professional qualification.Additional certification in Treasury or Corporate Finance preferred.

    2. Experience

    12–18 years in finance & accounts with at least 5 years in automotive dealership or OEM finance.Experience managing channel finance, floor plan funding and OEM claim reconciliation.Exposure to EV/PHEV inventory financing and incentive structures is an advantage.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    1. Financial Planning, Budgeting & MIS Reporting

    2. Working Capital, Inventory Funding & Treasury Management

    3. Statutory Compliance, Taxation & Audit Oversight

    4. OEM Claims, Incentive & Scheme Reconciliation

    5. Cost Control & Profitability Analysis by Business Vertical

    6. Banking & Channel Finance Relationship Management

    7. Internal Controls & Risk Management Framework

    8. Support to CEO on Investment & Capex Decisions (including EV charging infra)

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    i. Financial Health
    • Working capital days and interest cost as % of revenue
    • Inventory ageing and floor plan utilization
    • Debtor days and bad debt provisioning
    ii. Compliance & Controls
    • Statutory filing timeliness (GST, TDS, ROC)
    • Audit observations closure rate
    • OEM claims realization turnaround time
    iii. Profitability
    • Department-wise gross margin accuracy
    • Cost-to-revenue ratio
    • Budget variance analysis accuracy
    iv. Reporting & Governance
    • MIS/dashboard timeliness and accuracy
    • Banking limit utilization and renewal turnaround
    v. People & Governance
    • Leadership team retention and bench strength
    • Statutory, OEM audit and process compliance score

    5. Key Competencies

    Financial Acumen & Analytical RigorStatutory & Regulatory KnowledgeStakeholder & Banking Relationship ManagementProcess & Controls OrientationBusiness PartneringAttention to DetailIntegrity & Governance Mindset

    DepartmentCustomer Relations / Sales

    Position Overview

    The CR Head – Sales owns the end-to-end customer experience across enquiry to sale, delivery and post-sale touchpoints. They formulate team communication/interaction tools and unified funnels for the Dealership.

    1. Education

    Graduate in any discipline; MBA preferred.

    2. Experience

    10–14 years in automotive, retail, or hospitality customer experience/CRM functions.Prior experience building OEM customer-satisfaction audits and escalation management.5+ years of people management experience, including managing managers and multi-level teams.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    1. Design and govern the customer experience journey (enquiry to delivery to post-sale).

    2. Conduct Voice of Customer (VoC) analysis and drive process improvements.

    3. Coordinate cross-functionally with Sales, Service and F&I teams.

    4. Train/Coaching Skills

    5. Oversee data privacy and certification/compliance standards across the function.

    6. Own customer complaint resolution and escalation management at executive levels.

    7. Oversee CRM data quality and follow-up discipline across the funnel.

    8. Track dealership customer-satisfaction performance and drive audit readiness and report findings to leadership.

    9. Drive performance reviews, coaching and capability building for the CR teams.

    10. Represent the CR function in management, other and OEM review meetings.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Escalation ManagementSales Satisfaction Index Score (SSI)Net Promoter Score (NPS)

    5. Key Competencies

    Customer-first mindsetStrategic problem solvingOwnership and drive resultsTeam leadershipCommunication and inter-personal skillsStakeholder managementData analysis and CRM toolsAwareness of EV/Digital trends and product blocks

    Customer Relationship Manager (CRM) – Sales

    DepartmentCustomer Relations / Sales
    Reporting toCR Head – Sales
    Role impactDrive Customer Experience, Lead CRM Team & Strengthen Customer Loyalty
    DepartmentCustomer Relations / Sales
    Reporting toCR Head – Sales
    Role impactDrive Customer Experience, Lead CRM Team & Strengthen Customer Loyalty

    Position Overview

    The CRM – Sales leads a team of Customer Relationship Executives, ensuring lead and funnel discipline, consistent customer experience and CRM data quality across the enquiry-to-post-sale journey.

    1. Education

    Graduate in any discipline; MBA preferred.

    2. Experience

    5–8 years in customer relations, CRM, or client-relationship roles within retail, hospitality, or automotive.Minimum 3 years in a team-supervisory role.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    1. Monitor incoming leads across sources (walk-in, tele calling, website, digital/social, referrals) and ensure timely routing and follow-up.

    2. Conduct periodic audits, including mystery-shop checks, to ensure consistent customer experience standards across the team.

    3. Monitor CRM funnel health, call quality and appointment/test-drive show rates on a daily/weekly basis.

    4. Manage escalations and resolution of unresolved customer complaints.

    5. Conduct process audits and ensure OEM compliance readiness.

    6. Plan and manage customer engagement activities (previews, test-drive events, EV awareness drives).

    7. Manage referral network and repeat-purchase relationships.

    8. Coach and review the performance of CR Executives and support their appraisal process.

    9. Coordinate cross-functionally with Sales and Service teams.

    10. Oversee digital channels and online reputation management.

    11. Enforce customer data privacy and confidentiality policies.

    12. Report team performance and funnel MIS to the CR Head – Sales.

    13. Lead training and onboarding for new team members, including product/EV certification.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Escalation ManagementSales Satisfaction Index Score (SSI)Net Promoter Score (NPS)

    5. Key Competencies

    Team leadership and coachingProcess disciplineCustomer-first mindsetLead and funnel managementData analysis and CRM toolsWorking knowledge of EV sales considerations

    CHAPTER 3

    Recruitment and Selection

    "Acquiring the right talent is more than half of winning the game."
    Purpose:
    • Implementation of proven recruitment techniques across the network
    • Hiring of manpower with correct skillset
    Principles:
    • Usage of AI-enabled, recruitment techniques
    • Role-based recruitment process
    • Scientifically proven scoring methodology
    Benefit to Dealerships:
    • Plug-and-play recruitment application
    • Structured hiring across levels
    • Better quality of manpower hired results in higher retention rates
    • Technology leading to reduced cost of hiring
    Benefit to Customers:
    • Consistent experience
    • Higher satisfaction

    In this chapter, we will look at the standard hiring process to be followed throughout the network.

    3.1 Recruitment and Selection Process

    AIdentify the recruitment need & raise requirementReporting Manager
    BPrepare manpower requisition and get approval by DP/CEO/GMHR Manager
    CPublish the vacancy & collect resumesHR Manager
    DUpload resumes on Recruitment Management System (RMS) and get suitability scoreHR Manager
    EUpload documents and verify phone number using link shared by HR ManagerShortlisted Candidate
    FCheck and validate documentsHR Manager
    GAttempt psychometric and video-based assessment using link sharedShortlisted Candidate
    HIf test passed (≥70%) conduct interviewRound 1 - HR ManagerRound 2 - CEO/GM
    IIf Interview cleared (≥70%) approval round by JSW MotorsASM/RSM/ZSM/NSM
    JConduct reference and background checkHR Manager
    KDiscuss offer & issue LOI/JOL to candidateHR Manager
    LCandidate details pushed to DMS on joiningHR Manager

    Note: Orange box steps are to be done on the RMS tool

    A. Identify the recruitment need and raise requirement

    • Manpower requirement is provided by JSW Motors basis business volume and city category
    • Initiate the recruitment process as per target assigned

    B. Prepare manpower requisition and get approval by DP/CEO/GM

    • Reporting manager sends a manpower hiring request to the HR Manager via email
    • Once HR Manager has received the request, HR Manager fills annexure 3A, discusses and emails the filled form for approval to DP/CEO/GM
    • HR Manager gets form 3A approved before moving to the next step

    C. Publish the vacancy & collect resumes

    Internal sourcing

    Internal movement covers promotion, job rotation and transfer between outlets of the same dealership. The HR Manager must explore the following routes before external sourcing:

    SourceCostSpeed of hiringCandidate qualitySuitable for roles
    Internal job posting (IJP)LowFastHighAll roles
    PromotionLowMediumHighAll roles
    Job rotationLowFastVariableAll roles
    How to make an IJP
    • The HR Manager should use 3B. Internal Job Posting (IJP) Template to notify the position internally
    • The HR Manager should reach out to the reporting manager for any recommendation for promotion
    • The HR Manager should display the IJP on notice boards across organisation and share over digital platforms used by dealership
    Who can apply for an IJP
    • Completed at least 12 months in the current role
    • Not under a performance improvement plan
    • No open disciplinary case
    *Note that every internal candidate will also have to go through the same interview process (step D – step I) as listed in the flowchart above.
    How to apply for an IJP
    • Check the Internal Job postings on the notice board and dealer communication digital platforms
    • Apply for the position by filling up 3C. Internal Job Posting Application Form
    • Email the form to the HR Manager
    Points to note
    • The releasing manager should not intentionally hold/block an internal movement
    • A notice period of up to 15 days is suggested for effective handover of responsibilities
    External sourcing

    External sourcing starts only after an Internal Job Posting has been tried. HR Manager should use 3D. Recruitment ad template to advertise the open positions. Use the following table to select the source(s) for external sourcing:

    SourceCostSpeed of hiringCandidate qualitySuitable for roles
    Job portalsModerateFastModerateAll roles
    Online forums and professional groupsLowVariableModerateManager and above
    Social mediaHighFastModerateAll roles
    Recruitment consultantsHighFastHighManager and above
    Newspaper and local classifiedsModerateSlowModerateAll roles
    Job fairs and walk-in drivesModerateFastModerateAll roles
    Campus: degree and management collegesModerateSlowModerateEntry level roles
    Internal employees/prospects databaseLowModerateHighAll roles
    *ReferralsLowModerateHighAll roles
    *Employee referral programme
    a. What is the programme

    Under this programme, existing employees can refer suitable candidates and earn a referral bonus for every successful hire.

    b. Who may refer
    • All employees may refer candidates for any open position
    • The HR Manager, HR Executive and anybody on the interview panel can refer but cannot claim referral bonus for it
    • Referring a family member is permitted post mandatory relationship disclosure using annexure 3E
    c. How it works
    • The referring employee submits the 3E. Employee referral form with the candidate CV to HR
    • The referral bonus is released to referrer after the completion of 30 days of joining of the referred candidate
    • Referral bonus payment is made through payroll and is subject to tax deduction
    • Recommended payout ~INR 2,500 per candidate referred and joined

    D. Upload resumes on Recruitment Management System (RMS) and get suitability score

    HR Manager uses the Recruitment Management System (RMS) to screen and interview candidates.

    • Login to RMS portal and select the position and upload CV against that
    • RMS to generate a suitability score using AI integration
    • HR Manager reviews suitability score and sends link to the candidate to upload documents

    Guiding matrix for candidate suitability

    Candidate SuitabilitySuitability Score Range
    Highly suitable≥60%
    Suitable45-60%
    Not suitable≤45%

    E. Upload documents and verify phone number using link shared by HR Manager

    • Screened candidates receives a link from HR Manager through RMS to upload the necessary documents
    • The candidate uploads the documents and verifies phone number

    F. Check and validate documents

    • Once the documents are uploaded, the HR Managers receives documents on RMS
    • The HR Manager must review and approve the documents on RMS to move to the next step

    G. Attempt psychometric and video-based assessment using link shared

    • Upon approval, an online psychometric and video-based AI interaction is triggered to the candidate by RMS
    • Post completion of the assessment, a report is generated on RMS
    • HR Manager approves the candidates with more than 70% aggregate score for the next round

    H. If test passed (≥70%) conduct interview

    • Upon approving, a message is triggered to the interviewer as well as the candidate to undergo the interview round 1
    • Set interview schedule with the candidate and panel
    • Interview round 1 with the HR Manager: Conduct the interview using the following suggested checks and enter scores on RMS
    FactorWhat to check
    Team fitWho the candidate will report to and work within the team
    Anti-poachingWhether the candidate is with another JSW dealer partner
    Employment stabilityThe reason behind each job change, not the tenure alone
    Working patternWillingness to work weekends, festivals and month-ends
    Desire for growthWhat the candidate wants to be doing in two years
    LanguageLocal language ability for the market the outlet serves
    Distance and commuteDistance from the outlet and how they will travel each day
    Salary bracketExpectation against the approved band for the role
    Licence and drivingValid licence and actual driving ability
    Notice periodJoining date against the date the position is needed
    Reference checkThe outcome, including any note raised
    • HR Manager approves candidate to move to interview round 2
    • HR Manager should share annexure 3F with the interviewer(s) along with the candidate resume
    • CEO/GM conducts interview round 2 and enters scores on RMS
    • See annexure 3G for suggested interview questions
    • HR Manager reviews round 2 scores and move the candidates with ≥ 70% aggregate score to approval round

    I. If Interview cleared (≥70%) approval round by JSW Motors

    • Upon approving the candidate from round 2 by HR Manager, a message is triggered to the interviewer as well as the candidate to undergo approval round
    • This is the JSW Motors approval round and is conducted as per the below table:
    Interview for the Role of:JSW Motors Approving Authority
    Sales Consultant/Hostess/Corporate Sales ExecutiveASM
    Internal Dealer TrainerTraining Team
    Sales Manager/Customer Relationship Manager/Corporate Sales Manager/Team LeaderRSM
    GM/CR-HeadZSM
    CEONSM
    • HR Manager should share annexure 3F with the interviewer(s) along with the candidate resume
    • See annexure 3G for suggested interview questions
    • Evaluation scores are entered online (mandatory)
    • HR Manager initiates the next step of reference and background check
    • All applicants, whether chosen or not, must be informed of the outcome by the HR Manager within seven days of the interview

    J. Conduct reference and background check

    Reference check and background verification is done in-house by the HR Manager OR through an outsourced partner (refer 3H. Reference check form and 3I. Background verification form).

    What is verified
    CheckDocument and method
    IdentityAadhaar, PAN, passport or voter identity card
    AddressAadhaar, utility bill, rent agreement or bank statement
    Education10th and 12th marksheets, degree certificate and mark sheet for the highest qualification
    Previous employmentAppointment letter from the last employer, last three salary slips, relieving letter and previous one year’s Form 16
    Reference checkMinimum two references
    *Driving licenceValid 4-wheeler driving licence (permanent/ learning)
    Police verificationThrough the local police station
    Bank accountCancelled cheque or passbook copy in the employee’s own name
    Medical certificateMedical fitness report to be shared before date of joining

    *For SC, TL, SM, CSC, CSM, Car Evaluator, TD Co-ordinator, Valet/Driver, Security Guard

    K. Discuss offer & issue LOI/JOL to candidate

    • The HR Manager must finalise the salary structure as per Chapter 4
    • Prepare the letter of intent/job offer letter using annexure 3J
    • Email it to the DP for approval
    • Post approval, share the job offer letter with the candidate and get their signed acceptance
    • Upon acceptance from the candidate, HR Manager sends an acknowledgement message using the below template:
    Dear [Candidate Name], Welcome to [Dealership Name]. Thank you for providing acceptance on the offer letter. We are pleased to welcome you as [Designation Name] for JSW Motors. Your joining date as mentioned in the offer letter is [entre date] at [entre place] at [entre time]. We request you to carry the original copies of the documents submitted for verification. We look forward to welcoming you at [Dealership Name].
    • Keep the reporting manager copied in the acknowledgement email

    L. Candidate details pushed to DMS on joining

    • HR Manager accepts the candidate on RMS and pushes the details to DMS
    • DMS login is created and shared with the candidate on joining

    3.2 Best Practice

    • Get subscriptions of recruiter versions of job portals as it allows:
      • A faster hiring process by providing advanced candidate filtering options
      • Direct candidate messaging
      • CTC/ notice period-based filters
      • Automated sourcing tools to identify and contact top talent
    • When hiring next-generation talent:
      • Look beyond formal qualifications
      • Consider attitude, curiosity, learning ability
      • Consider candidates from industries like hospitality, retail, etc. with passion for cars
    • Maintain a backup pool to:
      • Track staff turnover and hire proactively
      • Aim to maintain a backup of at least 10% of the frontline staff
      • Keep in touch with old employees post their exit
      • Keep a list of ‘shortlisted but did not join’ candidates
    • Build a strong social media presence to:
      • Attract young and dynamic talent
      • Share team photos, employee stories, award ceremonies and appreciation posts
      • Present the dealership as a great place to work
    • Interaction via Online Channels:
      • Shortlisted candidates get an option to join HR round interview via video calls
      • Makes easier to reach candidate and speed up hiring process
    • Employee Referral Scheme:
      • Offer non-cash rewards (like movie tickets or family gifts) to top referrers

    CHAPTER 4

    Compensation, Benefits and Incentive Policy

    " Good compensation is not a luxury; it is a prerequisite for sustained growth."
    Purpose:
    • To establish a fair, structured and market-aligned compensation structure
    • Attract the right talent, retain strong performers and motivate the entire team
    Principles:
    • Fixed pay reflecting the role, responsibility and market benchmark
    • Variable and incentives tied directly to measurable performance outcomes
    • All statutory obligations on compensation and benefits are non-negotiable
    Benefit to Dealerships:
    • A structured pay framework reduces salary disputes
    • Performance-linked incentives drive the motivation to achieve dealership business target
    • Reduces attrition, which lowers the cost of hiring and training replacements
    • Statutory compliance protects the dealership from legal risk
    Benefit to Customers:
    • Fairly compensated employees deliver a better, more consistent customer experience
    • Well-aligned incentive structures lead to improved employee behaviour and customer relationship

    This chapter provides various components of the salary structure along with some benefits given over and above the fixed compensation.

    4.1 Components of Salary

    Total compensation has three components:

    PartWhat it includes
    Fixed payBasic salary, dearness allowance, house rent allowance and any other regular allowance
    Variable payMonthly or quarterly incentive as per policy, linked to performance
    Statutory benefitsProvident Fund, ESIC or medical insurance, gratuity, bonus

    Suggested Salary Structure

    Wage (Basic + Special Allowance)Statutory definition of wage as per The Code on Wages, 2019PF, Gratuity, Bonus baseMust meet state minimum wages
    HRA (Excluded from Wages)House Rent AllowanceNone — employer policy35% of Fixed CTC
    Conveyance Allowance
    (Excluded from Wages)    		Transport to/from workplaceNone10% of Fixed CTC

    Statutory BonusPayment of Bonus ActPayment of Bonus Act 19658.33%–20% of WagesMandatory if Wages ≤ ₹21,000/month
    Annual Payout, amount not to be specified in Appointment Letter
    SECTION 2 — DEDUCTIONS REFERENCE
    DeductionRateGoverning ActEmployer MatchNotes
    Provident Fund (PF)12% of WagesEPF & MP Act 195212% of Wages8.33% EPS + 3.67% EPF; voluntary above ceiling of Rs. 3000 per month
    ESI0.75% of WagesESI Act 19483.25% of WagesMedical cover for employee & dependants
    Wages < 21000 per month only eligible
    Professional Tax₹175–200/monthState PT ActsNilCheck Statewise Mandates
    TDS (Income Tax)As per income slabIncome Tax Act 2025NilBased on employee investment declarations
    GratuityNil (employer-borne)Gratuity Act 1972Not applicablePayable after 5 years for regular employees, 1 year for fixed-term Recommended to keep out of CTC

    *Please refer 4A for a sample salary slip

    Benefits

    BenefitApplicable to:Notes
    Provident fundAs required under the lawDeposited within the prescribed timeline, every month, without exception
    ESIC or medical insuranceESIC where applicable; otherwise, a group Mediclaim policyWhere ESIC does not apply, we recommend a group Mediclaim covering the employee, spouse and children (2 children up to the age of 25)
    GratuityAs required under the lawFixed-term contract employees now become eligible after one year rather than five
    BonusAs required under the lawAs per the compensation policy
    LeavesAs applicableEntitlements are in Chapter 12

    4.2 Perks

    See annexure 4B for the minimum facilities that should be in place at every outlet.

    Below perks are also offered in some cases:

    Perks
    Mobile allowance
    Travel + food allowance
    Transport at night for women
    Salary advance

    Interest free salary advance can be given as per the following guidelines:

    • Up to one month’s net salary, for a genuine need
    • Applicable for confirmed employees only
    • Recovered from salary in three to six instalments, agreed in writing
    • Must be approved by the Dealer Principal

    *Please refer to 4C. Advance Salary Request Form

    4.3 Changes in Salary

    Salary changes can be considered only in the following situations:

    WhenHow
    Annual incrementBased on performance review rating and business outcome of the organisation.
    PromotionSalary revised to the range for the new role, effective from the date of the promotion.
    Sideways movePay usually stays the same.
    Confirmation after probationAny pay change agreed at the time of the offer takes effect. Confirmation after probation is not automatically an increment.
    Counter-offer to retain somebodyIf the person is a high performer, salary correction can be done.

    4.4 Incentive Scheme

    It is a monthly performance reward program for achieving business targets.

    The below table lists down the process of rolling-out the scheme:

    DateActivityWho
    1stMonthly incentive scheme for the current month finalized (based on JSW Motors released monthly incentive scheme)Management
    1stScheme communicated to department heads using annexure 4DGM
    1stEmail the scheme to team members using annexure 4DGM
    2ndAnnounce and discuss the scheme in the morning meetingGM/SM
    Before 10thPerformance validation and payout calculation for previous month incentiveHR Manager & Finance
    Before 20thIncentive payout for previous monthPayroll / Finance

    Refer annexture 4E for a sample monthly incentive scheme.

    4.5 Best Practice

    • Dealers can provide special benefits like:
      • employee or immediate family discount on vehicle purchase, genuine accessories/merchandise
    • Link incentives to business priority:
      • introduce model-wise boosters for vehicles identified as priorities by JSW Motors
      • additional incentives may be offered for slow-moving inventory
    • Upon achieving 100% target, increase incentive progressively, the more one outperforms, the higher their incentive. This way strong performers will stay motivated even after achieving their monthly target.
    • Additional incentive for closing deals with zero discount

    CHAPTER 5

    Joining and Confirmation

    "Joining a new team isn’t about fitting into an existing culture, it’s about adding a unique perspective that makes the culture richer."
    Purpose:
    • To give every new hire a structured onboarding at the dealership
    • Set expectations during the probation period
    Principles:
    • A warm, welcoming and professional joining experience
    • Confirmation based on performance and behaviour
    Benefit to Dealerships:
    • Well-onboarded employees reach productivity faster
    • Structured joining and confirmation process promotes retention
    • Clear probation criteria prevent disputes during confirmation
    Benefit to Customers:
    • Prepared employees handle customer interactions with confidence

    The joining process for a new employee helps with their smooth onboarding. The following flowchart highlights the important steps.

    5.1 Joining and Induction Process

    APost offer acceptanceFix joining dateHR Manager
    BN-6 and N-3Send a reminder to the candidateHR Manager
    CN-2Remind the reporting manager about the new joinerHR Manager
    DNWelcome the new joinerHR Manager
    ENArrange necessary assets and accessHR Manager
    FNComplete joining formalitiesHR Manager
    GNIntroduce management, various department heads and the teamHR Manager
    HNIntroduce the Internal Dealer Trainer (IDT) and a team member as the buddyHR Manager

    ↓

    IN+1Explain the induction trainingHR Manager + IDT
    JConduct the 7-day induction trainingIDT

    A. Fix joining date

    • Finalise a joining date with the candidate and get the candidate acceptance on the offer letter

    B. Send a reminder to the candidate

    • Six days and then three days before joining, HR Manager sends a short message to the employee mentioning:
      • Dealership address (location map pin)
      • Dealership operational timing
      • Whom to contact upon arrival
      • Any documents to bring along, if applicable
      • Any other requirement as per the job role

    C. Remind the reporting manager about the new joiner

    • Two days before the candidate’s joining:
      • HR Manager sends a reminder to the reporting manager
      • The reporting manager informs the team about the new joiner

    D. Welcome the new joiner

    • HR Manager should be available on the joining day or make necessary arrangements in case of unavailability.
    • Welcome the new joiner with a warm gesture like a flower bouquet or chocolates.

    E. Arrange necessary assets and access

    • HR Manager must arrange the following assets upon joining:
      • Send a request to EDP to create the email and DMS access
      • Provide assets as required by the role holder
      • Share two sets of uniform
      • Issue the identity card
      • Add in the dealer communication groups

    F. Complete joining formalities

    • Complete all the necessary paperwork using annexure 5A with the new joiner like:
      • Signing code of conduct
      • Documentation of PF, ESIC and nominee details
      • Hand over the 5B appointment letter and take the signed copy back

    G. Introduce management, various department heads and the team

    • Arrange an introduction with:
      • Reporting manager and the team
      • Individual department heads
      • DP or GM

    H. Introduce the Internal Dealer Trainer (IDT) and a team member as the buddy

    • On the joining day, introduce the IDT and the new joiner.
    • The IDT will:
      • Act as the new joiner’s buddy during the induction period
      • Give a walkaround of the entire dealership premise
    • Also introduce a team member who the new joiner will shadow during the day-to-day customer interactions for the first two weeks

    I. Explain the induction training

    • On N+1 day, HR Manager and the IDT explain the 7-day induction process to the new joiner.
    • Induction training is:
      • Monitored by the HR department
      • Conducted by IDT
    • HR Manager informs:
      • Dealership operational hours
      • Salary date
      • Attendance and leave rules
    • IDT should:
      • Enrol the new joiner on the LMS
      • Confirm the induction course list
      • Create induction training batch in training management system

    J. Conduct the 7-day induction training

    • Following table gives a comprehensive list of trainings to be conducted during induction:
    DayThemeTopics to Cover
    Day 1Welcome to JSW MotorsJSW Group & JSW Motors introduction | Dealership introduction | Vision and values |Organisation structure | Introduction to team and department heads | Dealership tour | Buddy introduction |LMS enrolment | Code of conduct, grooming, data privacy and safety
    Day 2Know Your RoleJob description | Roles & responsibilities | Reporting structure | KPIs | Daily work routine | Responsibilities towards customers | Interaction with other departments (will differ from role to role) | Assessment 1
    Day 3Know Your ProductCurrent product range | Variants | Key features | Customer benefits | Product walkaround | FAB approach | Basic competitor understanding | Product demonstration practice
    Day 4Know Your Customer & Sales ProcessCustomer expectations | Complete sales journey | Enquiry handling | Need understanding | Product presentation | Test drive |Follow-up | Booking | Delivery | Customer complaint handling | Assessment 2
    Day 5Know Your Systems & ProcessesDMS basics | CRM basics | LMS | Attendance/leave system | Enquiry entry | Customer follow-up records | Documentation | Data handling | Basic process standards
    Day 6Learn on the FloorObserve real customer interactions | Practise greeting and need understanding | Product walkaround practice | CRM practice | Understand coordination with Finance, Insurance, Accessories, Exchange, Delivery and CRM teams
    Day 7Check Readiness & Set GoalsReview first-week learning | Short knowledge check | Product walkaround/role play | Employee questions | Manager feedback | Set performance KPIs | Confirm next learning actions | HR records induction completion | Assessment 3
    • After induction training completion, the new joiners are nominated for Level 1 or role-based training.

    5.2 Probation and Confirmation Process

    The recommended probation period is three months.

    Basis performance, the management will confirm, extend, or not confirm the employee.

    AN-15Initiate confirmation processHR Manager
    BN-10Reporting manager gives confirmation recommendationReporting Manager
    CNInform the employee about the outcomeHR Manager

    A. Initiate confirmation process

    • HR Manger initiates the 5C confirmation form duly filled and emails it to the reporting manager

    B. Reporting manager gives confirmation recommendation

    • Reporting manager:
      • Sends the confirmation form back to the HR Manager
      • Mentions performance, training completed, attendance and conduct
      • Gives a clear recommendation

    Either of the three outcomes below can be recommended by the reporting manager:

    OutcomeWhenWhat follows
    ConfirmedPerforming as per expectation, training complete, no conduct problem5D confirmation letter is issued
    ExtendedImproving but not as per expectationsExtended with written reasons and a clear improvement plan
    Not confirmedNot able to do the job even with support, or a conduct problemServices ended as per the notice period in the offer letter

    C. Inform the employee about the outcome

    • HR Manager should initiate a one-one-one discussion with the employee
    • In the discussion, share the outcome with the employee
    • Initiate the next steps according to the outcome – confirmed, extended, or not confirmed

    5.3 Best Practice

    • Create The Right Impression:
      • As the reporting date and time is decided in advance, new joiners should not be left to wait at the reception / lounge
      • HR Manager should personally coordinate and receive them in the designated area with a small pre-welcome act of presenting new joiner with a flower / plant / chocolate pack etc along with a standardized welcome card
    • Welcome Kit and Social Platforms:
      • Giving a welcome hamper containing & dealership co-branded utilities such as diary, pen, bottle, key chain etc is a best practice, encourage the employee to update information of their new role on social media and professional platforms with pictures
      • The dealership can also post a photo about the new joiner on their official social handle and wish them good luck in their new role
    • Publish Organization Announcement:
      • A new joiner announcement e-mailer should be circulated to everyone
      • The email can include the work experience, educational qualifications and department of the new joiner
    • Buddy Feedback:
      • Daily verbal feedback can be collected by the HR Manager from the IDT on the progress or challenges faced by the new joiner to support them in their new role

    CHAPTER 6

    Learning and Development

    “Training is not an expense, but an investment in building skilled people.”
    Purpose:
    • Develop employee capability to perform their role effectively
    • Provide relevant training to address performance and skill gaps
    • Support business development through performance excellence at individual level
    Principles:
    • Tech-enabled, role-specific, experiential learning and certification
    • Industry-leading learning pathway
    • Learning driven by business outcomes

    Benefit to the Dealer:

    • Improved sales, customer satisfaction and revenue
    • Improved sales techniques to close deals faster hence improving productivity
    • Higher employee engagement and retention
    Benefit to Customer:
    • Accurate product information and professional handling
    • Consistent experience across all touchpoints
    • Increased trust and confidence in the brand

    This chapter sets out how the HR Manager, and the Internal Dealer Trainer (IDT) drive the learning and development for the dealership staff.

    Learning design should be scientifically driven using the following techniques:

    • Addie instructional design model: Analyse, Design, Develop, Implement, Evaluate
    • 70:20:10 rule: Learn from experience, social interaction and formal training
    • Learning pyramid: Optimized retention through different learning methods
    • Klob’s experiential way: Focus on experiential learning
    • Kirkpatrick’s model: Evaluation of training effectiveness

    Types of training can be categorised as:

    • ILT – Classroom training as per the learning journey
    • LMS – Self-paced micro-learning
    • OJT – On-site training programs
    • Refresher trainings On product, process and soft skills

    6.1 Learner’s Journey

    JSW Motors designed a structured learner journey for each role as follows:

    6.2 Introduction to Training Management System

    • Training Management System is a comprehensive digital platform designed to manage the complete training journey for all relevant sales roles.
    • Features of Training Management System:
      • Real-time visibility of training calendar
      • Nominations
      • Attendance
      • Training status
      • Assessment results

    6.3 Monthly In-house Training Calendar Planning Process

    • The IDT conducts the Training Need Analysis (TNA) to prepare monthly training calendar.

    Sample Training Plan:

    Input from Previous Month’s TNA drives current month’s calendar

    6.3.1 Planning & scheduling refresher training sessions

    Scheduling Considerations

    • Avoid during festive seasons and outdoor/event activities
    • Ensure participants availability

    Participant Capacity

    • Define maximum capacity based on training mode and space constraints
    • Ensure effective knowledge transfer with appropriate trainer-to-participant ratio

    Session Duration

    • Maximum 2 hours per session
    • Optimal for maintaining engagement and retention while minimizing operational interruption

    Training Modes

    • On-the-Job Training (OJT) – practical, hands-on learning in the work environment
    • Observation-Based Coaching – supervised observation with feedback from trainer or coach
    • Classroom Training – instructor-led, structured learning sessions

    6.4 Non-availability/ Absenteeism for JSW Motors Trainings

    6.5 Failing an Assessment in JSW Motors Trainings

    • For assigned LMS e-learnings, retake is allowed on the platform
    • Participants failing the post-test for classroom training must undergo retraining in the next available batch within 30 days to achieve certification

    6.6 Introduction to Learning Management System (LMS)

    LMS is an app-based platform that enables continuous self-learning.

    Features of LMS:

    • Structured and Personalized Learning
      • Role-based plans for participants
      • What to learn and finish with progress visibility
    • Online Assessments & Knowledge Checks
      • Quizzes, pre/post-tests and periodic evaluations online
      • Capturing scores, attempts and completion
    • Digital Knowledge Library
      • One-stop searchable access to product details, SOPs, manuals, FAQs, reference guides
    • Newsletters, Bulletins & Communications
      • Circulars and product updates announcements
    • Surveys & Feedback
      • Online forms capture learner feedback
      • Training effectiveness
      • Content relevance

    Learning Path Flow:

    The HR Manager & IDT holds the governance for Learning and Development for in-house trainings.

    Governance cadence

    WhatFrequencyWhoHow to Conduct
    Training calendarMonthly, by the 25thIDTNext month module plan and employee nominations
    Training record updateWithin one day of any sessionIDTAttendance, assessment results, certification details
    Training delivery review with GMMonthlyIDT & HR ManagerEffectiveness, planned vs actual trainings

    What IDT reports to JSW Motors

    i. Training delivery coverage
    • Monthly training calendar planned vs actual trainings
    • Attendance status of various trainings conducted
    ii. Effectiveness
    • post-training assessment scores from trainings conducted
    • monthly training summary 6C

    6.8 Best Practice

    • Internal Dealer Trainer: HR department in close consultation with management needs
      • to ensure that IDT is selected strictly basis to core competencies
      • make this role aspirational and respected within dealership
      • discourage namesake appointment / job rotation to fill up this post
    • One product one week:
      • a short 10-question test is conducted every Thursday through an easy-to-use platform
      • each weekly test to be dedicated to single product or process
      • IDT to publish leaderboard by EOD
    • Local Speaker Sessions:
      • each city has accomplished professors, business leaders, administrators and government officials known for their hard work and achievements
      • dealerships should invite these local speakers for short leadership and professionalism sessions
    • LMS Dashboard:
      • leverage LMS dashboards to monitor training completion
      • assessment scores and certification status in real time

    CHAPTER 7

    Performance Management

    “Performance management is not a yearly review, it’s a daily conversation.”
    Purpose:
    • Structured review process to optimise individual performance
    • Alignment with goals, KPIs and targets
    • Document and formalise the assessment process
    Principles:
    • Goals are set at the start of the year and communicated clearly
    • Mid-year review and feedback is progressive and goal-oriented
    • Appraisals are free from bias and backed by data
    Benefit to Dealerships:
    • Performance leads to productivity
    • Enhanced operational efficiency
    • Empowers employee development and retention
    Benefit to Customers:
    • Accountable employees deliver a more consistent experience
    • Teams with clear KPIs resolve queries faster and close transactions more efficiently

    Performance management is:

    • career driven – driven by monitoring individual KPIs
    • business driven – activities to drive the business

    7.1 Career Driven Performance Management

    The performance of an individual is measured by following these 5 key steps:

    Chart 7.1 The Performance Management OR Appraisal Cycle

    7.1.1 Performance Management Process

    ADefine dealership’s annual goals and share with GM/SM/HRMCEO
    BConduct a meeting with all department heads to announce the goalsHR Manager
    CDraft SMART KPIs with targets, discuss with team and set expectationsReporting Manager
    DCommunicate the KPI targets to the employees and take their sign-off keeping HR Manager copied in the emailReporting Manager
    EHold quarterly and mid-year reviews with the employee and check KPIs progress using annexure 7BHR Manager + Reporting Manager
    FShare self-assessment against the KPIs at the end of annual performance review cycleEmployee
    GWrite the assessment against each KPI in annexure 7B and calculate the rating and gradeReporting Manager
    HHold the annual review meeting and share the grade with the employeeHR Manager + Reporting Manager
    IEmail the final grade to the employee and take their sign off with HR Manager copied in the emailReporting Manager + Employee
    A. Define dealership’s annual goals and share with GM/SM/HRM
    • Dealership Principal or CEO organise an annual meeting with the GM/SM/HRM to finalise the dealership goals as per their business plan
    B. Conduct a meeting with all department heads to announce the goals
    • The HR Manager organises a meeting with aa department heads
    • The goals are announced by the HR Manager
    C. Draft SMART KPIs with targets, discuss with team and set expectations
    • Each employee’s reporting manager defines the target against the KPIs as per the dealership’s goals
    • Follow the SMART framework while setting KPIs:
      • S – Specific – exactly what you want to accomplish
      • M – Measurable – how success will be measured
      • A – Achievable – realistic with available resources
      • R – Relevant – goal aligns with the job role
      • T – Time-bound – set a clear deadline for completion
    • The targets are then discussed and agreed with the employees in a one-on-one meeting with the reporting manager
    D. Communicate the KPI targets to the employees and take their sign-off keeping HR Manager copied in the email
    • The target KPIs are emailed to the employee by the reporting manager keeping HR Manager in copied in the email
    • The employee must provide their acceptance on the set performance target
    • The KPIs must then be added in form 7B by the reporting manager and emailed to the HR Manager
    E. Hold quarterly and mid-year reviews with the employee and check KPIs progress using annexure 7B
    • For April to March cycle:
      • a. Quarterly reviews are held in June and December
      • b. Mid-year review is held in September
      • c. Annual review is held in March
    • Two weeks before the review is due, HR should remind the reporting manager to conduct the review meeting
    • Reporting manager should schedule a one-on-one review meeting with the employee
    • All reviews must be conducted on Business Results dashboard available through DMS to track the KPIs
    • Review performance expectations against the set KPIs:
      • where each KPI stands, in numbers
      • what is going well, said plainly and specifically
      • what must change in future and what support the person needs to do it
      • whether any KPI needs revising because the dealership goal has shifted
    • During the review meetings, reporting manager must fill form 7B and email it to the HR Manager
    • Document what was agreed on an email with the employee with the HR Manager in cc (sample below) summarizing meeting conclusions about:
      • Favourable results
      • Performance issues
      • Action plan

    Subject: Quarterly/Mid-year/Annual Performance Review Summary To: [Employee Email Address] Cc: [HR Manager Email Address]

    Hi [Employee First Name],

    Thank you for participating in your [quarterly/mid-year/annual] performance review. As discussed, this email summarizes our meeting to ensure we are fully aligned moving forward.

    a. Favourable results

    Your hard work reflected in several areas this quarter:

    • KPI 1
    • KPI 2
    • KPI 3

    b. Performance issues

    You finished the quarter averaging 2 unit per month, while our standard is a minimum of 6 units per month.

    c. Action plan

    We have committed to the following action plan over the next XX days:

    • ________________
    • ________________

    We will do a quick review of XXX to track your progress and ensure you have the support you need to hit these numbers.

    I have great confidence in your ability to hit these targets and I am fully committed to helping you succeed. Please reply directly to this email to confirm that this accurately reflects our conversation and your commitment to the plan.

    Best regards,

    [Your Name] [Your Title, e.g., Sales Manager] [Dealership Name]

    F. Share self-assessment against the KPIs at the end of annual performance review cycle
    • Two weeks before the annual review is due, HR Manager reminds the reporting manager to complete the annual performance review
    • The reporting manager requests the employee to share their self-assessment against the set KPIs
    G. Write the assessment against each KPI in annexure 7B and calculate the rating and grade
    • Reporting manager fills up the assessment against each KPI in annexure 7B
    • From the rating, calculate the grade as per the table below:
    RatingGradeNameIncrement %What it means
    5A+OutstandingTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomePerformance is well beyond the agreed KPI.
    4AExceeds expectationsTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomePerformance is consistently better than the agreed KPI.
    3B+Meets expectationsTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomeKPI is achieved as expected.
    2BNeeds improvementTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomeFalls short, needs a written plan and support.
    1CUnsatisfactoryTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomeNot performing as per the agreed KPIs and cannot continue as it is.
    H. Hold the annual review meeting and share the grade with the employee
    • Conduct a one-on-one annual performance review meeting with the employee
    • During the meeting discuss the employee’s annual performance and share the grade with them.
    • Increment and promotion decisions are taken based on these ratings and grades
    • A rating of 1 goes to the PIP process below
    • Nobody can be rated 4 or 5 if they have an open disciplinary matter or an integrity concern
    I. Email the final grade to the employee and take their sign off with HR Manager copied in the email
    • The reporting manager emails the summary of the annual performance review meeting to the employee along with their grade
    • Obtain the employee’s acknowledgement on the final grade shared with them
    • HR Manager must be kept copied in all performance review related emails

    7.1.2 Handling Underperformance with a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)

    If the reporting manager sees the employee struggling to achieve KPIs, follow the below steps:

    AState the performance issue directly to the employee in the performance review meetings and follow meeting summary emailsReporting Manager + HR Manager
    BIdentify the root cause and create a corrective action plan with a defined timeline of coaching/mentoringReporting Manager + HR Manager
    CIf the employee’s performance does not improve in the established timeline, create a PIP using annexure 7CReporting Manager + HR Manager
    DShare the PIP with the employee in a one-on-one meetingReporting Manager
    FConclude the outcome of the PIP and if performance has not improved, proceed to termination as per notice period in the offer letterReporting Manager + HR Manager
    EConduct a weekly PIP review meeting with the employee in the HR Manager’s presenceReporting Manager

    7.2 Business Driven Performance Management

    Regular governance activities must be run to drive the business towards achieving its goals, like:

    • daily morning meeting - conducted by SM/GM with all sales and customer relationship team members
    • weekly meeting - conducted by all department heads with their respective teams
    • fortnightly meeting - conducted by GM with SM, TLs and CRM
    • monthly meeting - conducted by DP/CEO with GM/SM/HR Manager

    For details on these business-driven performance management activities, please see annexure 7D.

    CHAPTER 8

    Career Progression

    " The expert in anything was once a beginner."
    Purpose:
    • Provide employees a visible career path within the dealership
    • Retain strong performers by investing in their growth
    Principles:
    • Career pathway is defined
    • Promotions are criteria-based, not only tenure-based
    Benefit to Dealerships:
    • Transparent career paths are one of the strongest retention tools
    • Internal promotions cost less than external hiring and carry lower onboarding risk
    Benefit to Customers:
    • Experienced, tenured staff understand the customer base and deliver more personal service
    • Continuity in the team builds long-term customer trust in the dealership

    This chapter talks about the different career progression path at dealerships.

    8.1 Career Progression Routes

    These are the usual career progression paths at a dealership and can be followed if there is a vacancy. Note that the time for movement to a new role is only for guidance.

    Work AreaEntryNext step
    (~2-3 years)    		Supervisory
    (~4-6 years)    		Leadership
    (~8-10 years)
    Sales floorSales ConsultantSales Team LeaderSales ManagerBusiness Head/GM/CEO
    Customer relationsHostess / ReceptionistCRE SalesCRM SalesCR Head (Sales)
    Sales supportDelivery CoordinatorCar Registration & DeliveryCar Finance / Car Insurance
    Used carsCar EvaluatorUsed Car ConsultantUsed Car Manager
    MarketingMarketing ExecutiveMarketing Manager
    AccountsCashierAccountantAccounts & Finance Head
    HR and systemsHR Executive / EDP ExecutiveHR Manager

    Chart 8.1 Career routes Note: This is the table for the same department movement. Lateral movement is also possible which is explained further in this chapter.

    8.2 Promotion Process

    • Promotions are decided at the annual review, with increments, unless a vacancy comes up mid-year
    • Lateral movement is not always a promotion and is covered later in this chapter
    01Follow the IJP process listed in chapter 3HR Manager
    02Propose the employee for promotionReporting Manager
    03Check eligibilityHR Manager
    04Follow assessment process defined in chapter 3Reporting Manager with the HR Manager
    05Take promotion decision upon clearing the assessmentReporting Manager with the Business Head
    06The decision is put in writing by sharing annexure 8A with a revised JD, KPIs and salary structureHR Manager
    07Inform the employee about the outcome with the reasons and share promotion letter, new JD and KPIsReporting Manager with HR
    08Handover the old role and any training needed for the new oneReporting Manager and IDT/ HR Manager

    Eligibility for Promotion

    EligibilityHow it is checked
    Time spent in the current role
    • Minimum 12 months
    • Only confirmed employees should be considered
    Performance
    • Rating of 4 or more in the last annual review. Rating not below 3.5 in the past two years
    • No pending integrity or disciplinary action
    • Manager feedback captured in the last annual review
    Certification
    • All the required training levels should be completed for the current role
    • Leadership trainings completed before any people-management role

    8.3 Lateral Movement

    • Lateral movement refers to inter-department movement
    • Following employees can opt for lateral movement by applying for an IJP posted by the HR Manager as detailed in chapter 3 section 3.1.3:
      • employees seeking career growth
      • employees seeking a new role more closely aligned with their skillset
    • Eligibility to apply for lateral movement is the same as given in the internal movement section of chapter 3.

    CHAPTER 9

    Employee Engagement, Rewards and Recognition

    "People work for money, but go the extra mile for recognition, praise and rewards."
    Purpose:
    • Create a workplace where employees feel valued, motivated and connected
    • Employee engagement through consistent and meaningful reward programs
    Principles:
    • Rewards & recognition to be timely and transparent
    • Linked to KPIs and behaviours
    • Both monetary and non-monetary recognition
    Benefit to Dealerships:
    • Engaged employees are more productive and contribute to long-term business success
    • Dealership known for rewarding employees becomes a best place to work
    Benefit to Customers:
    • Motivated manpower delivers stronger customer trust and loyalty
    • Stable, motivated teams provide a consistent and dependable customer experience

    This chapter covers the suggested employee engagement, rewards and recognition programs for a dealership.

    9.1 Employee Engagement Activities

    • Employee engagement activities are driven by the HR Manager
    • Employee Engagement Calendar is published in December month of the previous year on digital platforms and also placed on the notice board

    9.1.1 Suggested engagements calendar

    ActivityGuidelinesPurposeArranged ByAttended By
    Birthday celebration.Frequency – once every month
