    CHAPTER 10

    Discipline and Conduct

    "Talent might make you good but it’s your attitude and work ethic that will make you great."
    Purpose:
    • Maintain a professional, respectful and safe working environment
    • To ensure that disciplinary action is consistent, fair and documented
    Principles:
    • Conduct standards apply equally across all levels
    • Every employee entitled to be heard before any action is taken
    • The disciplinary process escalates progressively
    Benefit to Dealerships:
    • A culture of accountability improves overall discipline and reduces conflict
    • Clear conduct framework protects from reputational and possible legal risks
    • Disciplinary processes reduce the chance of wrongful practices
    Benefit to Customers:
    • Customers like to interact with staff who represent the dealership's values
    • Better protection of personal and financial information

    This chapter outlines the code of conduct expected from the employees.

    10.1 Code of Conduct

    The following code of Conduct applies to all dealerships and its employees and sets out the ethical requirements that are mandatory. If something feels wrong or inappropriate - even if it's not specifically written here - trust that instinct and think before you act.

    1. Respectful Conduct & Appearance

    • Arrive at work on time, providing notice to the reporting manager in the event of unavoidable delays
    • Wear clean and approved company uniforms
    • Maintain a neat, well-groomed personal appearance
    • Keep individual desks, sales areas, service bays, and communal spaces neat and organized
    • Restrict phone usage during working hours and customer interactions
    • Treat all everyone with dignity regardless of their designation, gender, religion, caste, or background
    • No bullying, no inappropriate jokes, no harassment of any kind
    • If you face or witness any misbehaviour, discrimination, or harassment at work, report it immediately to HR or your manager

    2. Transparency & Customer Service Standards

    • Always give complete and accurate information about:
      • Prices
      • Loan terms
      • Vehicle specifications
    • No hidden charges or surprises at delivery time
    • Only sell or fit authorized accessories and spare parts
    • Give written estimates before doing any additional work and get customer approval

    3. Data Privacy & Confidentiality

    • Keep all customer documents (Aadhar cards, PANs, salary slips, addresses) secure
    • Never share customer details outside the dealership
    • Don't discuss customer's:
      • Purchase details
      • Loan information
      • Personal matters with other customers or on social media

    4. Health & Safety

    • Follow all safety rules in the workshop - wear proper safety gear, handle tools correctly and never take shortcuts that could cause accidents
    • Report any unsafe conditions immediately (broken equipment, oil spills, electrical issues, expired fire extinguishers) before someone gets hurt
    • Follow all traffic rules during test drives and vehicle movements; ensure all vehicles have valid insurance, pollution certificates and proper documentation

    5. Integrity & Anti-Corruption

    • Never accept or give bribes, cash gifts, or kickbacks to/from customers, vendors, bank staff, or RTO officials
    • Don't take money from the cash counter, claim false expenses, or manipulate bills and invoices for personal benefit
    • If you see theft, fraud, customer cheating, safety violations, or any wrong behaviour, speak up - report it to your manager, HR, or use anonymous email / written letter
    • Don't help customers submit fake documents for loans or registration and don't use fake/duplicate parts - these are criminal offenses

    6. Conflict of Interest

    • If you have family members or personal business relationships with vendors or customers, inform the HR Manager immediately
    • Don't do side businesses or part-time work that competes with the dealership
    • Do not use company time and resources for personal work

    10.2 Serious Misconduct Leading to Possible Immediate Termination of Services

    Money and property theft

    • Stealing anything that belongs to a customer or dealership - money, documents, belongings left in their vehicle during service

    Financial dishonesty with customers

    • Keeping a portion of the customer's payment for yourself without the dealership's knowledge

    Taking illegal benefits from vendors

    • Accepting money, commissions, gifts, or any favours from finance companies, insurance agents, part suppliers, or brokers in exchange for giving them business
    • Giving company business to a vendor because they're paying you personally, not because they're the best choice

    Faking business records

    • Creating fake booking entries for vehicles that were never actually sold, or inflating numbers to meet targets
    • Changing, hiding, or lying about any official record - sales data, service reports, attendance, stock registers, or customer complaints

    Document forgery

    • Signing a customer's name on any document without their knowledge or permission - loan papers, delivery documents, service approvals, anything
    • Creating fake documents like salary slips, ID proofs, or address proofs for customers or for yourself

    Misusing customer information

    • Selling customer contact lists, addresses, or financial details to other businesses, marketing companies, or individuals
    • Sharing confidential customer data outside the dealership for any reason other than official business purposes

    Lying during hiring

    • Giving false information in your job application or interview - fake degrees, inflated previous salary, hiding that you were terminated from your last job, or providing a fake experience certificate
    • Using someone else's documents or qualifications to get hired

    Sexual harassment

    • Making unwanted physical contact, sexual comments, inappropriate messages, or requests for sexual favours from any colleague or customer
    • Showing obscene material, making lewd gestures, or creating a hostile environment for anyone based on their gender (details covered separately in Section 10.3)

    Threatening or violent behaviour

    • Using abusive or threatening language toward customers, colleagues, or managers
    • Physical violence of any kind - pushing, hitting, threatening to harm someone, or destroying things in anger

    Coming to work intoxicated

    • Reporting to work under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or any substance that impairs your ability to work safely and professionally
    • Consuming alcohol or drugs during work hours, including lunch breaks

    Dangerous or illegal driving

    • Driving any dealership vehicle or customer vehicle without a valid driving license
    • Rash driving, over speeding, racing, or doing stunts with dealership or customer vehicles

    Deliberately damaging property

    • Intentionally breaking, scratching, or vandalizing dealership property - vehicles, equipment, computers, showroom furniture
    • Damaging a customer's vehicle deliberately during service or test drive

    Unexplained long absence

    • Disappearing from work for more than 2 days without informing anyone - no call, no message, no explanation - leaving your team and customers stranded

    Working for a competitor or dual employment

    • Taking another full-time or part-time job with a competing dealership, brand, or automotive business while employed here
    • Running your own competing business (like vehicle reselling, spare parts shop) while working for the dealership without disclosure and approval

    Deliberate insubordination

    • Openly refusing to follow a clear, reasonable and legal instruction from your manager or supervisor
    • Repeatedly and intentionally ignoring direct orders that are part of your job responsibilities

    Criminal activity or actions harming JSW Motors reputation

    • Being involved in any illegal activity that becomes known publicly and damages the JSW Motors brand image
    • Any behaviour - on duty or off duty - that gets reported in news or social media and brings disrepute to the company

    Sabotage or espionage

    • Deliberately sabotaging dealership operations, passing confidential business information to competitors, or helping competitors harm the business

    Tampering with safety equipment

    • Disabling, removing, or tampering with safety devices, fire extinguishers, CCTV cameras, or security systems

    Fraudulent warranty or insurance claims

    • Filing fake warranty claims with JSW Motors or false insurance claims to benefit personally or help a customer fraudulently

    Bringing weapons to workplace

    • Carrying firearms, knives, or any weapons onto dealership premises (except legally authorized security personnel)

    Allowing unauthorized people to work

    • Letting friends, family, or unauthorized people handle dealership operations, use dealership systems, or access restricted areas in your place

    10.3 The Disciplinary Process

    The process below is a step-by-step guide to handle any disciplinary issue allowing fairness and transparency in the approach ensuring all decisions are based on facts.

    AVerbal Counselling
    BWritten Warning (First)
    CWritten Warning (Final)
    DSuspension Pending Investigation
    EShow Cause Notice & Inquiry
    FTermination of Employment

    A. Verbal Counselling

    • For first-time minor issues like occasional lateness, dress code violations, minor customer service lapses, or small procedural mistakes
    • The manager has a one-on-one conversation with the employee
    • Employee explains what went wrong

    B. Written Warning (First)

    • When the verbal counselling didn't work and the behaviour repeated, OR for more serious issues like repeated tardiness, unauthorized absence, poor performance after coaching, or not following standard procedures / code of conduct
    • A warning letter 10B is sent stating what rule was broken with its consequences and what's expected going forward
    • Employee signs it acknowledging it was received

    C. Written Warning (Final)

    • When the first written warning didn't result in improvement and the issue happened again, OR for serious misconduct like insubordination, significant policy violations, or behaviour that risks customer relationships or safety
    • A second and final written warning is given using 10B
    • This one clearly states that if the behaviour happens again, employment will be terminated

    D. Suspension Pending Investigation

    • When there's a serious allegation that needs thorough investigation - like theft, fraud, harassment, violence, or major safety violations - and it's better for everyone if you're not at work while facts are gathered
    • Employee pending investigation is asked to stay home (with or without pay, depending on the situation) while the dealership investigates
    • Employee will be sent a 10C suspension email
    • During this time, employee cannot contact customers/colleagues about work matters

    E. Show Cause Notice & Inquiry

    • For serious or gross misconduct, or when earlier steps haven't worked and termination is being considered. This ensures you get a fair hearing and the dealership has proper documentation before making a final decision
    • A "show cause notice" is sent listing the allegations against and asking employee to explain their side in writing within a set timeframe (usually 48-72 hours)
    • If needed, a formal inquiry meeting is held where employee can present their version or bring witnesses
    • Management reviews all evidence before coming to a decision

    F. Termination of Employment

    • When all previous steps have been exhausted without improvement, OR immediately for gross misconduct offenses listed in the immediate termination section (theft, fraud, violence, etc.)
    • If the evidence supports that employee committed serious misconduct or didn't improve despite multiple warnings, employment is terminated
    • A termination letter is issued stating the reasons, final settlement details and last working day

    Things to be careful about

    • Do not decide the outcome before completing the investigation
    • Maintain proper records of all documents, including notices, responses, investigation records, findings and final decisions
    • Do not discuss the matter around the dealership
    • Do not let a manager handle a case where they are personally involved
    • Apply the same standard to everybody regardless of the position or seniority
    • If a criminal offence has taken place, such as theft, the dealership may also file a police complaint. The internal process still must be followed

    Appeal

    If an employee believes a disciplinary decision is unfair, they may submit a written appeal to the HR Manager or Dealer Principal within seven days. The appeal will be reviewed and a final decision will be shared in writing within fifteen days.

    10.4 POSH: Prevention of Sexual Harassment

    This is governed by the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

    What counts as sexual harassment

    Any unwelcome behaviour of a sexual nature. This includes:

    • Physical contact or advances
    • Asking for or demanding sexual favours
    • Sexually coloured remarks, jokes or comments about a person's body
    • Showing pornography
    • Any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature, including messages, photographs and social media

    The workplace includes the showroom, the workshop, the stockyard, the parking area, a customer's home during a visit, a test drive, an event, an outing and a work trip. It also covers work-related messages and calls outside office hours.

    The internal committee

    Every dealership with ten or more employees must have an Internal Committee also called as IC. This is a legal requirement, not a recommendation.

    PositionWho
    Presiding OfficerA senior woman employee of the dealership
    MembersAt least two employees committed to the cause of women, or with experience in social work or law
    External MemberOne member from an NGO or a person familiar with issues relating to sexual harassment. Not an employee of the dealership
    CompositionAt least half of the members must be women
    TermThree years

    Where the dealership has no senior woman employee, the Presiding Officer may be nominated from another outlet of the same dealer partner.

    How a complaint is handled

    StepWhat happensTime
    1The complaint is made in writing to the IC using annexure 10E. If the woman cannot write it herself, the IC must help her put it in writing.Within 3 months of the incident, extendable by 3 months
    2The IC may first offer conciliation, if the woman asks for it. No money settlement is allowed as the basis of conciliation.Before the enquiry
    3The IC holds an enquiry. Both sides are heard. Confidentiality is maintained throughout.Completed within 90 days
    4The IC gives its report to the Dealer Principal.Within 10 days of completing the enquiry
    5The Dealer Principal acts on the recommendation.Within 60 days of the report
    6Either side may appeal.Within 90 days

    While the enquiry is going on

    • The person may ask for a transfer, for the other person to be transferred, or for leave of up to three months. This leave is in addition to her normal leave.
    • The identity of everybody involved is kept confidential. Discussing the case around the dealership is itself a disciplinary matter.
    • No action of any kind may be taken against the woman for having complained. Any pressure or unfair treatment after a complaint is major misconduct.

    What the dealership must do

    • Display the names and contact details of the IC members where everybody can see them
    • Explain POSH to every new joiner during induction, including men
    • Run an awareness session at least once a year through certified POSH trainer
    • Train the IC members through certified POSH trainer
    • File the annual return with the District Officer
    • Include a POSH section in every appointment letter and the conduct code

    A knowingly false complaint made to harm somebody is also a disciplinary matter.

    10.5 Grievance Handling

    A grievance is any work-related problem, concern, or complaint that's bothering an employee’s and affecting their job, dignity, or workplace experience. The steps taken to resolve the grievance is also beneficial to ensure a healthy workplace environment.

    AInformal Resolution
    BFormal Written Grievance
    CAcknowledgment & Initial Review
    DInvestigation
    EResolution & Communication
    FAppeal (if not satisfied)
    GFinal Review & Closure

    A. Informal Resolution

    • Within 3 days of the issue occurring the employee talks to their Reporting Manager and explains what happened

    B. Formal Written Grievance

    • If talking to the manager didn't help, within 7 days, employee submits written grievance to HR Manager
    • Write what happened (with dates and details), who was involved and what is to be done about it
    • Submit it in person, by email, or through the grievance box, if available

    C. Acknowledgment & Initial Review

    • Within 2 working days of receiving the grievance, HR acknowledges that they've received the complaint
    • HR does a review to understand the issue, decide its seriousness and who should investigate

    D. Investigation

    • Within 7-10 working days from acknowledgment, HR/Investigating Officer investigates by talking to the concerned party, talking to the person complained about (if applicable), interviewing witnesses and reviewing any evidence
    • Everything is kept confidential

    E. Resolution & Communication

    • Within 3-5 working days after investigation is complete, HR Manager communicates decision to employee
    • Based on the investigation, management decides what action to take - like counselling, changing a policy, taking disciplinary action, or explaining why no action is needed

    F. Appeal (if not satisfied)

    • If not satisfied with the resolution, an appeal can be made to a higher authority (like the dealer principal) within 7 days of receiving the resolution
    • The appeal must be put in writing explaining why the decision was wrong

    G. Resolution & Communication

    • The higher authority reviews the original complaint, investigation findings, appeal and any new information
    • Within 15 working days from receiving the appeal, a final decision is made which is communicated to relevant parties in writing

    Important Points to Remember

    • Every grievance is taken seriously – Raising a genuine grievance through proper channels will not result in any punishment, transfer, salary cut, or bad treatment. If anyone retaliates against anyone for complaining, that itself is a serious violation.
    • Confidentiality is maintained – The complaint is handled discreetly. Only people who need to know (to investigate or resolve it) will be informed.
    • False complaints have consequences – If investigation proves employee deliberately made a false complaint to harm someone or create trouble, the said employee may face disciplinary action yourself. But this only applies to intentionally false complaints, not genuine concerns that turned out to be misunderstandings.
    • Emergency issues – For serious matters like harassment, violence, theft, or safety emergencies report immediately to HR, the dealership head, or reach out to the Dealer Principal/CEO.
    • Anonymous reporting option – Employee can use anonymous email to report serious violations without revealing their identity, though it may limit how thoroughly the issue can be investigated.
    • Keep records – Save copies of written grievance, any emails and the responses. If things get complicated later, these will be proofs of what was said and when.

    Grievance committee

    If required by law, the dealership must establish a Grievance Committee with representatives from both employees and management. The committee should also include adequate representation of women. HR is responsible for monitoring legal requirements and ensuring the committee is formed in a timely manner.

    CHAPTER 11

    Employee Exit Management

    "People leave companies but they remember how they are treated on their way out."
    Purpose:
    • To ensure employee exits are handled professionally and fairly
    • Apply appropriate insights to improve the overall employee experience
    Principles:
    • Exit managed through a defined process and approval
    • Fully documented and recorded exit with confidentiality
    • Full and final settlement completed within a defined timeline
    Benefit to Dealerships:
    • Proper handover process protects dealership operations and customer relationships
    • Reason of exit helps retention improvement initiatives
    • Safeguards dealership from legal and compliance risk
    Benefit to Customers:
    • Maintain continuity of customer relationships through handover

    In this chapter, we will understand a standard exit management process that must be followed across all JSW Motors dealerships.

    11.1 Exit Process

    AResignation by employee to the reporting and HR Manager or dealership takes termination decisionEmployee/ HR Manager
    BOne-on-one meeting with the employeeReporting Manager
    CDecide if the employee is to be retained or notReporting Manager + HR Manager
    DOne-on-one meeting with the employeeHR Manager
    EResignation acceptance email sharedReporting Manager + HR Manager
    FHandover list preparedEmployee with Reporting Manager
    GRole handover completedEmployee and successor/ Manager
    HConduct exit interview 3 days before the last working day.HR Manager
    IClearance form completed with all assets handed over.HR Manager/Accounts
    JFull and final settlement, relieving letter and experience letter sharedHR and Accounts

    A. Resignation by employee or dealership takes termination decision

    • Employee shares resignation email to reporting and HR Manager
    • Dealership takes termination decision due to conduct or performance issues

    B. One-on-one meeting with the employee

    • On resignation day, reporting manager arranges a one-on-one meeting with the employee

    C. Decide if the employee is to be retained or not

    • Reporting and HR Manager together decide if the employee is to be retained

    D. One-on-one meeting with the employee

    • HR Manager also arranges a one-on-one meeting with the employee to understand any concerns

    E. Resignation acceptance email shared

    • HR Manager must provide acceptance on the resignation email within 3 working days using annexure 11A
    • Last working day as per the notice period must be mentioned in the email:
    StageNotice Period
    During probation15 days
    After confirmation, Customer Facing and Support roles30 days
    After confirmation, Leadership roles60 days
    • Notice can be shortened by mutual agreement in writing
    • Notice can be bought out by the employee or next employer or waived off by the dealership

    F. Handover list prepared

    • The handover should include the transfer of:
      • -key responsibilities
      • -ongoing tasks
      • -critical contacts
      • -important documentation
    • Knowledge transfer sessions should be conducted by the reporting manager with the receiving employee
    • Return or transfer ownership of company assets
    • The resigned employee and the employee taking handover signs the annexure 11B

    G. Role handover completed

    • Handover of all roles and responsibilities including active leads handover must be completed 5 days before the last working day

    H. Conduct exit interview

    An exit interview gives an opportunity to share feedback on overall employment experience

    It is to be done by the HR Manager 3 days before the last working day around the following lines:

    • Reason for leaving
    • About the role & manager in terms of expectations, support & guidance
    • About the work environment
    • About the growth & development
    • About compensation and benefits
    • Preference for come back and recommendation to friends & colleagues
    • Open feedback

    Use annexure 11C to capture exit interview response.

    HR should read all the exit interviews forms and share the findings with the Dealer Principal.

    I. Clearance form completed

    • DMS access removed on the last working day by the EDP
    • All assets like laptop, sim card, etc. must be handed over to the HR Manager before exit
    • Post handover of assets, annexure 11B will be completed by the HR Manager, Accounts and Business Head

    J. Full and final settlement done

    • Salary dues must be settled within 2 days of last working day
    • Gratuity, where payable, is released with F&F settlement
    • Provident Fund is claimed by the employee and HR can help with the paperwork
    • Earned incentive for tenure completed months is paid as part of full and final settlement
    • Any advance or dues are adjusted
    • The relieving and experience letter (annexure 11D) are given as soon as the settlement is done

    11.2 Manpower Attrition

    • Once employee code is generated, that employees is considered for attrition monitoring
      • Employee in DMS -> counted in
      • Employee out of DMS -> counted out
    • The roles to be considered for calculating manpower attrition are:
      • Team Leader
      • Sales Consultant
      • Corporate Sales Executive
    • Manpower attrition is calculated on a monthly rolling basis (last 12 months)
    • The HR Manager needs to find out the reason for attrition during exit interview and share it with management for improvement
    • Use the below formula to calculate manpower attrition rate:

    Manpower Attrition = Manpower Left / (Manpower Opening + Manpower Joined) x 100

    Example: ABC Automobiles | Attrition Calculation | Dec 2025

    Total SC, TL and CSE Left (Jan 25 – Dec 25) = 36

    Total Manpower Joined (Jan 25 – Dec 25) = 40

    Opening Manpower (1st Dec 25) = 68

    Attrition Dec 2025 = [ 36 / ( 40 + 68 ) ] X 100 = 33%

    IMPACT OF ATTRITION

    An employee’s productivity starts declining three months before their exit. Hiring their replacement takes one month while the new joiner takes another three months to reach maximum productivity.

    CHAPTER 12

    Organisation Policies

    "Policies make the foundation that guides behaviour, ensures fairness, and protects an organization."
    Purpose:
    • Establish clear, standardised policies that govern the day-to-day working
    • Ensure statutory compliance and provide a fair framework to protects employer and employee
    Principles:
    • Statutory obligations are non-negotiable for all policies
    • Every employee made aware of applicable policies on their first day
    • Policies updated regularly as per changes in the business or law
    Benefit to Dealerships:
    • Clear policies reduce disputes, grievances and ambiguity in day-to-day operations
    • Statutory compliance protects from penalties and litigation
    • Employees who understand the rules work with confidence
    Benefit to Customers:
    • A well-governed dealership is more reliable
    • Structured internal operations produce fewer errors and a dependable experience

    This chapter covers all the policies that are necessary for dealership operations.

    12.1 Working Hours, Attendance and Week-off Policy

    Purpose:

    • To set standard working hours, attendance, late coming and week off arrangements
    • Ensure the dealership operates consistently and every employee knows what is expected

    Scope: Applies to all employees across all functions and outlets of the dealership

    Working hours

    ItemRecommended
    Working hours9 hours a day including the break
    Showroom timing9:30 am to 7:00 pm
    Lunch break45 minutes
    Week offOne full day every week, on rotation. Usually, a weekday for customer facing team members, because weekends are working days
    Working on the week offCompensatory off within 30 days, or overtime pay as per law
    OvertimePaid at twice the ordinary rate OR as the law requires. It must be recorded

    Roster

    • The manager maintains the roster on DMS considering the working days required to run the dealership operations.
    • Showroom coverage comes first. The roster must always leave enough people on the floor on Saturday and Sunday.
    • If the weekly off is changed at short notice, the employee is told the reason and given another day off that week.
    • During a festival period or a big campaign, week offs may be adjusted.

    Marking attendance

    • Use biometric system only.
    • Attendance is marked when arriving and when leaving.
    • For staff who go out for RTO work, bank work, home visits or deliveries, he/she should send a note to the reporting manager/HR, so they are not shown absent.

    Attendance records

    • Leave record must be updated.
    • HR closes attendance for the month by the date fixed for payroll, usually the 26th.
    • Any correction must be requested before the closing date. After payroll is processed, it is adjusted the subsequent month.
    • Records are kept as the law requires and may be kept in electronic form.

    If you cannot come to work

    • Inform the reporting manager before the day starts.
    • Then apply for leave in the system on the same day or the next working day.
    • Absent without informing your manager is treated as leave without pay and repeated cases are a disciplinary matter.
    • Absent for a period more than 3 working days without information is absconding which may lead to disciplinary action.

    Late coming

    SituationWhat happens
    Late more than three times in a monthHalf day will be marked in the system
    Habitually lateWritten warning from HR Manager and disciplinary action

    Disclaimer: HR to follow territory and state labour laws.

    12.2 Leaves and Holiday Policy

    Purpose:

    • To give every employee a clear entitlement to all types of leaves and holidays
    • Defined process for leave application and approval

    Scope: Applies to all full-time employees of the dealership

    TypeHow many daysFor what
    Earned Leave12 days a yearPlanned leave, holidays, personal work. Applied for in advance
    Casual Leave5 days a yearShort, unplanned needs. Usually, one or two days at a time
    Sick Leave5 days a yearIllness. Medical certificate needed if more than 2 days together
    Maternity Leave26 weeksFor the first two children. 12 weeks for the third onwards, as per law
    Compensatory OffAs earnedFor working on a week off or a holiday. To be used within 30 days

    Applying for leave

    Type of leaveHow much notice
    Earned leave, 1 to 3 daysAt least 3 days before
    Earned leave, more than 3 daysAt least 15 days before
    Casual leaveAt least 1 day before, or the same morning in an emergency
    Sick leaveInform the manager and apply on return
    Maternity leaveAt least 8 weeks before

    Approving leave

    • The reporting manager approves within two working days. HR records it
    • Leave can be refused only for a genuine business reason and the reason must be explained
    • If leave is refused, offer another set of dates
    • Before going on leave, the person hands over their work in progress jobs to a named colleague

    Other leave FAQs

    QuestionAnswer
    Can earned leave be carried forward?Yes. Up to 24 days. Anything above is encashed or lapses as per the state rule
    Can leave be encashed?Yes. Earned leave only, at the time of exit
    Do casual and sick leave carry forward?No. They lapse at the end of the year
    Can casual leave be added with earned leave?No. Casual leave is meant for unplanned needs
    Is a holiday inside a long leave counted?A holiday or week off falling in the middle of earned leave is counted as leave
    Leave during notice period?Only with the manager’s written agreement
    Leave during probation?No. In emergency cases, only post manager’s approval

    Holidays

    • The dealership publishes its holiday list for the year before the year starts
    • National holidays must be given: 26 January, 15 August and 2 October
    • Other holidays are chosen based on the local festivals in that town
    • Around 10 holidays in the year are normal
    • A showroom may stay open on a festival day because customers want delivery on that day. Staff who work get compensatory off or holiday pay as per law

    Disclaimer: HR to follow territory and state labour laws

    12.3 Travel Policy

    Purpose:

    • To define business travel, expenses approval and reimbursement

    Scope: Applies to all employees who travel for business purposes, whether locally or outstation

    Local travel

    Travel within the dealership city limits

    How they travelWhat is paidRecommended
    Own two-wheelerPer kilometre₹ xx per km
    Own carPer kilometre₹ xx per km
    Auto, taxi, bus, metroActual fareWhere receipt available
    Dealership vehicleFuel as per actualLogbook entry needed
    • Local travel is claimed monthly, with the date, place and purpose written for each trip
    • The claim goes to the reporting manager and is paid within 15 days
    • Travel between home and the dealership is not claimable. That is normal commuting

    Outstation travel

    Outstation travel must be approved in advance by the Business Head and by the Dealer Principal for leadership roles.

    CategoryModeStayDaily recommended allowance
    JuniorBus, or train in sleeper or 3ACBudget hotel₹ xxx a day
    MiddleTrain in 3AC or 2ACBudget hotel₹ xxx a day
    SeniorTrain in 2AC, or air where the distance and time justify itBusiness hotel₹ xxx a day

    Daily allowance covers food and small expenses. If the dealership or JSW Motors is providing meals, the allowance is reduced accordingly. Amounts are recommendations only and to be confirmed based on local requirements.

    How to claim

    • Get written approval before travelling. An email or a signed travel form is enough.
    • Take a travel advance if needed. Ask HR at least two days before.
    • Keep the tickets and bills. A claim without a bill is settled only at the Business Head’s discretion.
    • Submit the claim within 7 days of coming back. Claims submitted after 30 days are not accepted.
    • The manager checks and approves and accounts settles it within 15 days.
    • Adjust any advance taken against the claim.

    Simple rules on travel

    • Travel by the cheapest sensible option.
    • Two people travelling to the same place should travel together and share a room where it is appropriate.
    • Claim only what was actually spent. A false claim is major misconduct under Chapter 10, however small the amount.
    • Personal travel added to a business trip is at the employee’s own cost.
    • Anybody driving on dealership work must hold a valid licence. Traffic fines from careless driving are the employee’s own liability.
    • Settle claims quickly.

    12.4 Uniform Policy

    Purpose:

    • To ensure all staff present a professional and consistent image
    • Reflects the JSW Motors brand standard at all times

    Scope: Applies to all employees across all functions and outlets of the dealership

    Uniform components (as applicable)

    ItemQuantity
    Shirt / T-Shirt2 pairs at joining and replacement after completion of a year
    Trousers2 pairs at joining and replacement after completion of a year

    Modification guidelines

    Employees may add personal touches to their appearance within these guidelines:

    • Small, non-obtrusive accessories such as watches, bracelets, or earrings
    • Well-groomed hair styles that project a professional image and reflect well on the dealership as brand ambassadors

    Issuance and maintenance

    • New employees receive 2 sets of complimentary, designated uniform on joining
    • Existing employees receive 1 set of complimentary, designated uniform in each year of active service
    • Additional uniform can be purchased through the internal store or ordering system
    • Uniform maintenance is the responsibility of each employee
    • Damaged or worn-out uniforms must be replaced by the employee promptly

    Enforcement

    • This policy is enforced by reporting managers and supervisors
    • Failure to comply may result in disciplinary action, including fines or deductions
    • Exceptions based on religious or medical requirements may be granted on a limited-time basis, subject to approval by HR and senior management
